strengths: Significance: Combining learned coarse-grained PMFs with tractable flow proposals is a useful direction for incorporating explicit-solvent effects while reducing sampling dimensionality. Reusing proposals to compare candidate PMFs is also practically appealing.

Empirical merits: The biased-data experiments demonstrate meaningful improvements on alanine dipeptide. For the Heavy Atom mapping, reweighting reduces JS divergence from 0.0505 to 0.0090 and PMF error from 2.5861 to 0.2758 (Table 6). Both coarse-graining resolutions outperform the reported generalized Born baselines on these metrics.

Presentation and reproducibility: The workflow is clearly organized, and the appendices provide substantial architecture, optimization, simulation, and hardware details. The clipping ablation transparently exposes an important failure mode.

Limitations and ethics: The manuscript acknowledges the difficulty of selecting collective variables and treats larger-system applications as future work. The broader-impact discussion is proportionate to the demonstrated research; no material ethical concern is apparent.
weaknesses: Soundness—central exactness claim: Equation 17 targets the learned distribution p_eta, not the true coarse-grained marginal p. An approximately accurate PMF does not make estimates unbiased under p, contrary to Section 3.3 and the framing in the abstract and Figure 1. Increasing the number of generated samples does not remove PMF approximation error. Moreover, self-normalized importance sampling is generally biased at finite sample sizes even with an exact target.

Soundness—essential truncation changes the target: Appendix G.2 discards the largest 1% of weights. A fixed discarded fraction generally introduces persistent asymptotic bias. This is consequential: without clipping, Table 6 reports essentially zero ESS and severe errors, including PMF error 261.7 for biased Core Beta proposals. The successful results therefore establish a useful truncated heuristic, not the advertised asymptotically exact sampler. The source of the extreme weights and the resulting bias need substantially stronger analysis.

Theory does not establish the claimed training-to-accuracy connection: Proposition 1 is a valid conditional LSI bound, but its force-error expectation is under p_eta, whereas ordinary force matching trains under p* and ESFM under the biased data distribution. No distribution-shift bound connects those objectives to the stated guarantee. Proposition 2 concerns biased equilibrium ensembles; its applicability to the finite, evolving WT-MetaD trajectories requires conditional-equilibration evidence that is not provided.

Significance and evaluation: Experiments cover only a two-dimensional potential and alanine dipeptide, so scalability to larger molecular systems remains untested. There is no matched comparison against direct enhanced-sampling reweighting or simulation under the same learned PMF. These baselines would distinguish the benefit of the flow sampler from the benefit of ESFM itself. For flows trained on unbiased data, Table 6 shows improved PMF error but slightly worse JS divergence after reweighting.

Efficiency accounting is incomplete: Table 1 presents flow training and inference as the total, excluding PMF training, which adds 1.88 hours for Core Beta and 4.11 hours for Heavy Atom (Table 5), as well as data generation. The reported dimensionality-dependent inference savings are useful, but an end-to-end comparison at matched statistical accuracy is needed to support the broader computational advantage.

Reproducibility and technical presentation: The public-code footnote provides only https://github.com/. The manuscript does not explain the replication procedure underlying its error bars or sufficiently specify histogram/binning and zero-density handling for the reported metrics. Algorithm 1 also uses ||grad U_eta - F_proj|| squared, contradicting the plus sign required by Equations 13 and 16. This sign discrepancy must be resolved to make the implementation unambiguous.

Originality: The contribution primarily integrates established flow matching, importance sampling, and ESFM; Propositions 2 and 3 are explicitly attributed to prior work. Such integration can merit acceptance, but here the limited evaluation and unresolved exactness claims prevent it from establishing a sufficiently reliable advance.
